correctness.rationale: The claim specifies n>=4, unordered collision-free points, the full dihedral action, and rational coefficients. The equivariant Abrams model is appropriate because every rim triangle has three edges. Exact cell counts are c0=n(n+1)/2, c1=2n(n-1), c2=n(3n-7)/2. A general no-two-cycle argument fixes a spoke then a rim edge: coefficients of squares involving each edge must form a one-cycle in a path, and hence vanish, so H_2=0 integrally. Connectivity and Euler characteristic yield dim H_1=n+1. A complete six-case signed cellular trace calculation gives each D_n character value and its complex irreducible decomposition; the graph-cycle trace comparison proves H_1(X;Q)=H_1(W;Q)+epsilon_s as rational modules. The finite-group quotient transfer yields the rational orbit-space consequences. The embedded verify.py checks 1628 group elements for n=4..40 and full boundary ranks; this finite evidence is corroboration, not the proof of all n.

originality.rationale: The claim is the infinite wheel family's actual D_n action on ordinary unordered two-particle first homology, not the rank or vanishing H_2 already covered by major general/graph-specific works. Inspected 2014 Theorem 4 gives only abstract H_1 and wheel Y-phase equivalence up to sign; 2019 wheel section gives nonequivariant homology. The published wheel D_n record treats a different Morse complex; the two-point sign-Borel–Moore record treats a different homology theory. Explicit reflection-class traces and module decomposition are not statements in the inspected sources. Unindexed equivalence or a short implication from a naturally equivariant extension of known exchange-phase constructions remains a real risk.
residual_risks: A broader graph-configuration equivariant theorem in unindexed literature may specialize to this D_n character.

The known planar triconnected anyon and graph-cycle decomposition may permit an elementary equivariant refinement using embedding orientation, even though that refinement is not stated in the inspected primary works.
Index searches do not establish global publication priority, and no independent expert priority review was performed.

value.rationale: The wheel graph is the canonical basic family of planar 3-connected graphs, and its dihedral action reflects actual graph symmetries of collision-free particle motion. A complete infinite-family group character and rational module decomposition are natural topology invariants, finer than the established Betti number. The two reflection conjugacy types in even wheels act with distinct negative traces, unlike their uniform odd-rim trace; the canonical extra anyonic line carries the reflection sign. Consequently exactly two rational first-homology directions survive cyclic rotations but none survive full reflections, making the ordinary full-symmetry quotient rationally acyclic. This is substantive structured symmetry information rather than a random finite parameter or a restatement of ranks.
